stories.headline: Cheaper AI review needs a quality ledger

source.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization

read_evidence.scope: Complete engineering report: cost history, context and cache accounting, code-level reductions, model and effort experiments, shadow migration, latency percentiles, acted-on findings, blinded review methodology and acknowledged regressions.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: Cloudflare cut average AI code-review cost from $2.43 to $0.77 and median latency from 4:09 to 1:32 by trimming duplicate context, reducing model calls, changing model and effort choices, and simplifying reviewer code. Blinded checks found important code-quality findings held roughly steady, while medium-effort security and performance reviewers still lost useful findings.
stories.why_it_matters: Treat token cost, latency and review quality as one evaluation. Replay identical repositories across model, effort and context changes; track acted-on findings and blinded importance ratings, then reject savings that merely suppress valuable security or performance feedback.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 20 stories examine reward-hack training, predictive analytics, AI record provenance, agent handoffs and pre-action supervision.
stories.image_alt_intent: A code-review pipeline narrows repeated context and model calls into lower cost and latency gauges, while a separate quality ledger preserves acted-on findings and blinded importance checks.

stories.headline: GRAFT routes bad behavior into removable parameters

source.title: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It

read_evidence.scope: Complete research article: reward-hacking motivation, gradient-routing method, RETAIN and FORGET adapters, anchor environment, Qwen3-8B results, six toy environments, 32B SFT result and explicit limitations.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: Anthropic-affiliated researchers propose GRAFT, which routes gradients from monitor-flagged behavior into a FORGET adapter removed after training instead of penalizing detected hacks. In a Qwen3-8B arithmetic environment, ablation nearly eliminated measured hacking while preserving gains. The study remains preliminary: monitors were simple, tasks small, and suitable anchor environments may be difficult to construct.
stories.why_it_matters: Replicate GRAFT only in a contained training study. Predefine held-out hack tests, compare penalties and prompting baselines, measure task loss after ablation, and document whether the monitor, anchor environment and model scale resemble the intended deployment.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 20 stories examine inference economics, predictive analytics, AI record provenance, agent handoffs and pre-action supervision.
stories.image_alt_intent: A training graph routes flagged trajectories into a removable FORGET adapter and clean trajectories into retained parameters, followed by held-out hack and task-performance evaluation.

stories.headline: An AI business record needs its origin trail
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers

source.title: The missing chain of custody for enterprise AI — Why organizations must preserve the inputs, context and audit trail behind AI-generated business records

read_evidence.scope: Complete attorney analysis: AI records as ESI, Rule 37(e), prompts and source versions, model and system instructions, human revisions, legal holds, vendor retention, reconstruction limits and proportional preservation.

source.freshness_reason: This 120-hour expert analysis remains within the permitted 168-hour window and was selected for its concrete, source-specific governance checklist after fresher sources lacked equivalent preservation detail.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

coverage_labels: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.summary: Reuters Legal commentary argues that consequential AI-generated business records may require more than the final document. Prompts, retrieved source versions, model identifiers, system instructions, intermediate outputs, human edits, approvals and triggered actions can determine whether a record is explainable or defensible. The author recommends proportional preservation, updated legal holds and vendor checks rather than retaining every interaction indefinitely.
stories.why_it_matters: Classify AI uses by consequence, then preserve the minimum origin package for high-risk records: inputs, versions, outputs, edits, approvals and actions. Test whether vendors can export that package before procurement, because rerunning a prompt cannot reconstruct historical context reliably.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 20 stories examine inference economics, reward-hack training, predictive analytics, agent handoffs and pre-action supervision.
stories.image_alt_intent: A consequential AI report links backward to versioned prompts, sources, model settings and system rules, then forward to human edits, approvals and automated actions in an auditable chain.

stories.headline: Move an agent session into the editor without losing context

source.title: How to continue a GitHub Copilot app session in VS Code

read_evidence.scope: Complete six-minute tutorial: session transfer, preserved conversation and worktree, line-by-line diff review, continued prompting, manual edits, local testing and pull-request update.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: GitHub’s tutorial shows how to open a Copilot app session in VS Code while retaining its conversation, code changes and working context. The handoff lets an agent complete broad work remotely before a developer inspects the diff, continues the discussion, edits files and runs local tests. Pushing remains tied to the session’s pull request.
stories.why_it_matters: Use session transfer as a review boundary. Confirm the expected branch and worktree, inspect every changed file, rerun project checks and make manual corrections before updating the pull request; preserved context should accelerate review, not substitute for it.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 20 stories examine inference economics, reward-hack training, predictive analytics, AI record provenance and pre-action supervision.
stories.image_alt_intent: A remote agent session carrying conversation, plan and worktree passes into an editor where a developer reviews the diff, runs tests and decides whether to update the pull request.

stories.headline: Build a pre-action review Agent Skill for internal agents

read_evidence.scope: Complete official essay: agent identities and permissions, cross-layer signals, dynamic risk context, supervision before action, deterministic containment, traceability and practitioner judgment, with product-vision limitations.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: Microsoft frames internally deployed agents as active enterprise participants that need identities, containers, permissions and continuous cross-layer observation. Its Project Perception vision combines signals from identity, data, endpoint, network, cloud and runtime to assess risk before actions, contain behavior and preserve traceability. The article describes an approach, not independently measured deployment outcomes or universal controls.
stories.why_it_matters: Turn the control sequence into a read-only review skill: identify the agent and intended task, gather current signals, compare proposed action with permissions, and return allow, contain or escalate. Keep enforcement external and require practitioner judgment for ambiguous risk.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 20 stories examine inference economics, reward-hack training, predictive analytics, AI record provenance and agent handoffs.
stories.image_alt_intent: A pre-action review skill collects identity, data, endpoint, network, cloud and runtime signals, compares intent with permissions, then returns allow, contain or escalate to an external control.
stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable, read-only pre-action review procedure grounded in Microsoft’s October 19 agentic-insider control sequence. Create a skill named `agent-action-review` that accepts agent identity, intended task, proposed action, target resource and current cross-layer signals. Verify identity and permission scope; compare the action with task intent; record relevant identity, data, endpoint, network, cloud and runtime evidence; classify the result as ALLOW, CONTAIN or ESCALATE with reasons. The skill never changes permissions or executes the action. Test three fixtures covering an allowed read, an overprivileged write and ambiguous intent. Require external deterministic enforcement and named practitioner approval for every ESCALATE result.
